labels.label: theo:rep
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is correct. The theorem is printed as false on 2A₂+1, and the ℤ₂ reading of A₂ is fixed by the dispatch and disclosed in the checklist row and the REPORT questions. STATEMENT. theo_rep elaborates to Set.BijOn rep (RepDomain ℤ_[2]) RepSeq ∧ Set.InvOn repInv rep (RepDomain ℤ_[2]) RepSeq ∧ Set.BijOn repInv RepSeq (RepDomain ℤ_[2]). Here rep x = (p n x)ₙ, RepSeq = {q | q 0 = 0 ∧ StrictMono q} (the printed codomain, with ↗↗ read as strictly increasing), and repInv q = −inv3 · ∑' n, 2^{q n}·inv3ⁿ (the printed formula, with inv3 = the inverse of the unit 3, three_mul_inv3). The sum is a genuine sum on RepSeq (summable_rep, terms of norm ≤ 2⁻ⁿ). On RepDomain the total T, a, p are the paper's (a_eq_nu2, T_unique), so rep is the printed φ there. IS RepDomain EXACTLY THE CLAIMED COMPLEMENT? Yes. RepDomain = {x odd | ∀ k, 3Tᵏx+1 ≠ 0}. Since 3 is a unit in ℤ₂, 3y+1 = 0 iff y = −1/3, so RepDomain = 2ℤ₂+1 minus {x | ∃ k, Tᵏx = −1/3}. For odd x the iterates before the first visit to −1/3 are paper-defined, so this is the backward orbit under the paper's partial T as well. It is not a convenient smaller set: repInv_image proves repInv '' RepSeq = RepDomain ℤ_[2], so RepDomain is the largest set on which the printed φ⁻¹ can be a two-sided inverse. The bijection is non-vacuous because RepSeq ∋ id. With the printed inverse, this is the strongest true form. REFUTATIONS. neg_inv3_not_mem_image proves Odd(−inv3) ∧ −inv3 ∉ repInv '' RepSeq. It is also true by hand: S(q) = 1 would force Σ_{n≥1} 2^{q_n}/3ⁿ = 0, but that sum is 2^{q_1}/3·(odd). neg_third_preimage was checked by hand: 3y+1 = 2ᵏ·(−1/3), so T(y) = −1/3. rep_printed_false is ¬∃ φ : ℤ_[2] → ℕ → ℕ, MapsTo φ {x | Odd x} RepSeq ∧ LeftInvOn repInv φ {x | Odd x}. This is not a strawman. The printed statement (φ : 2A₂+1 → RepSeq bijective with inverse the formula) implies such a φ exists. The negation quantifies over every φ, not only over values of the undefined p_n, so it refutes the printed theorem whatever completion is chosen. Finding 2 (the printed proof l.92–95 derives only x = φ⁻¹(φ(x)), never φ(φ⁻¹ q) = q) is true. It is a gap in the proof, and the REPORT words it as one, not as a falsity. Injectivity (rep_injOn, eq_of_p_eq) holds in every IsZ2Ring, by Krull. The one overstatement is that neg_third_preimage's docstring and the REPORT claim ν₂(3y+1) = k, which the declaration does not state (minor finding 2).

labels.label: cor:ring_following_equivalent_enumerate
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial. I agree that it should not be marked, but for two reasons where the REPORT gives one (see minor finding 1). STATEMENT. periodic_a_iff_periodic_T: ∀ {A} [CommRing A] [IsZ2Ring A] (x : A) (n : ℕ), (∀ k, a (k+n) x = a k x) ↔ ∀ k, T^[k+n] x = T^[k] x. Two companion forms cover the other readings. eventually_periodic_a_iff_periodic_T is the same for every fixed start index K, which also gives the ∃K form. minimal_period_a_iff_minimal_period_T is the least-period form. So under the integral reading of 'ℤ/2ℤ-ring' (OQ-42 (a)), the statement is at least the printed one under each reading of 'periodic of period n'. There is no 2 ≠ 0, so ZMod 2 is included. Every x ∈ A is covered. On every x where the paper's sequences exist (x odd, orbit avoiding −1/3), the total T and a are the paper's T_A and a_n, so there it is the printed equivalence verbatim. SHOULD IT BE MARKED? Not yet. (1) OQ-42 (a). IsZ2Ring includes IsDomain, and l.52 does not. Without integrality the corollary is false at a point where the paper's own maps are defined. Take B = ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ and x = (1, 0). B is noetherian, B/2B ≅ ℤ/2ℤ, 2 ≠ 0, and (1,0)(0,1) = 0. 3x+1 = (4,1) has ν₂ = 2 and a unique quotient, so T(x) = (1,1) and T(1,y) = (1,1). Then a_k(x) = 2 for every k (period 1), but T(x) ≠ x. A /tmp probe proved this in Lean, axioms standard; the probe is deleted. (2) OQ-42 (d). At even x (outside the printed domain 2A+1) and on the backward orbit of −1/3 when 3 is a unit, the printed sequences do not exist. There, the truth of the statement depends on how they are completed. The Lean completion follows the formula: T(−1/3) = 0, which lies outside the printed codomain 2A+1, and with it the equivalence holds. A completion inside the printed codomain, for example T(−1/3) := 1 and a₀(−1/3) := 2 in ℤ₂, gives a ≡ 2 (period 1) while T(−1/3) ≠ −1/3. That is (i) without (ii) at x = −1/3. This is argued, not formalized. So the printed statement under the paper's definitions is settled only after both rulings. Once OQ-42 (a) is ruled integral and OQ-42 (d) is ruled (total maps, or orbits avoiding −1/3), the existing declaration certifies the row with no new Lean. The docstring and SCOPE text ('proved with no added hypothesis', Rep.lean:15; 'holds for every x ∈ A, ring and n', :62) is true only under OQ-42 (a)'s taken reading.

labels.label: cor:ring_periodic_minimal_period
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial. That is correct: the corollary is false as printed at i = j, and the i ≠ j form is a correction. FINDING 3 CHECKED, TRUE. cor_ring_periodic_minimal_period_printed_false negates the printed universal: every B : Type with IsZ2Ring, x, n with IsPeriodicPt T n x, 0 < n, no smaller positive period, α : ℤ → ℕ agreeing with a(x) on ℕ, ∀ i j ∈ [1, n], A_iⁿ − A_jⁿ ≠ 0. It uses the printed Aun and no i ≠ j. Refuting the Type-0 instance refutes the printed claim. The witness is the cycle (1) of ℤ: T(1) = 4/4 = 1, n = 1, i = j = 1, and α u = a_{u.toNat}(1) = 2 lies in (ℕ*)^ℤ. ℤ is integral with 2 ≠ 0, so the witness satisfies every reading of the hypotheses. CORRECTED FORM. Aun_sub_ne_zero and AunAlt_sub_ne_zero carry the printed hypotheses ('n-periodic' as Tⁿx = x, 'minimal' as no positive period m < n, i, j ∈ ⟦1, n⟧ as integers) plus i ≠ j. They conclude (A_iⁿ : ℤ) − A_jⁿ ≠ 0 for the printed Aun (product to n−1−k, i.e. range (n−k)) and for AunAlt (range (n−1−k), i.e. product to n−2−k), the two OQ-43 readings. I checked the cycle identity by hand. Aun_cast_eq: reindex A_uⁿ = Σ_j 3^{n−1−j}2^{p_{j+1}(x_u)}, then apply lem:base at n+1 and 2^{p_{n+1}}T^{n+1} = 2^{p_n}(3Tⁿ+1). This gives A_uⁿ = 2^{p_n(x_u)}(3x_{u+n}+1) − 3ⁿ(3x_u+1). On a cycle this is (2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ)(3x_u+1), and AunAlt is (2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ)x_u (Aun_cast_of_cycle). 2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ is odd because p_n ≥ 1, x_1, …, x_n are distinct by minimality, and cancelling 3 and 2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ uses the domain. The α weakening (any extension of a(x) to ℤ) is harmless: only indices in ⟦1, 2n−1⟧ enter. Non-vacuity: cycle_neg_five proves T(−5) = −7 and T(−7) = −5 with least period 2, which I checked by hand, so the i ≠ j hypotheses are satisfiable. The 'IsZ2Ring A; no 2 ≠ 0' hypothesis row has the same undisclosed integrality as the first corollary (minor finding 1).

findings.where: Rep.lean:38 (checklist row 'A a ℤ/2ℤ-ring, x ∈ A (both corollaries) | ✓ carried'), Rep.lean:15 and :62–64; REPORT labels[1].hypotheses[0] and questions[0], labels[2].hypotheses[0]
findings.what: The REPORT says cor:ring_following_equivalent_enumerate is 'proved with no added hypothesis' and that 'the author may rule the row closed without a corrected statement' once OQ-42 (d) is ruled. That holds only under OQ-42 (a)'s taken reading. IsZ2Ring includes IsDomain, which l.52's definition of a ℤ/2ℤ-ring omits; only l.50 says 'integral'. The integrality is load-bearing. B = ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ is noetherian, has B/2B ≅ ℤ/2ℤ (quotient_two_of_parity) and 2 ≠ 0, but (1,0)(0,1) = 0. For x = (1,0), 3x+1 = (4,1) has ν₂ = 2 and a unique quotient by 4, so T(x) = (1,1) = T(1,y) for every y. Hence a_k(x) = 2 for all k (period 1), but T(x) ≠ x. The first corollary therefore fails in B, at a point where the paper's own T_B and a_n are defined, so this is not a junk artefact. A /tmp probe proved it in Lean against Syracuse.T and Syracuse.a (statement: IsNoetherianRing B ∧ Nonempty ((B ⧸ span{2}) ≃+* ZMod 2) ∧ (2 : B) ≠ 0 ∧ (1,0)·(0,1) = 0 ∧ (∀ k, a (k+1) x = a k x) ∧ ¬ ∀ k, T^[k+1] x = T^[k] x), axioms standard; the probe is deleted. The row is partial and unmarked, so nothing is over-certified. But the disclosure names only OQ-42 (d) as what the mark waits on, and the checklist calls the hypothesis carried. The second corollary's row has the same omission: its proof cancels 3 and 2^{p_n} − 3ⁿ in a domain. A side observation for OQ-42 (a), outside this target's labels: the same B shows that l.51's 'noetherian … excludes this situation by Krull' fails without integrality, since ⋂ 2ⁿB = 0 × ℤ/3ℤ ≠ 0.
findings.fix: In Rep.lean's checklist and in the REPORT hypotheses of both corollaries, add the row 'A integral (l.50; not in l.52's definition), OQ-42 (a) | ⚠ strengthened via IsZ2Ring'. Change 'no added hypothesis' (Rep.lean:15, REPORT labels[1].questions[0]) to 'no hypothesis beyond IsZ2Ring (OQ-42 (a))', and name OQ-42 (a) beside (d) as what the mark waits on. Optionally prove the ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ witness in Rep.lean as a finding about the l.52 definition. It takes about 60 lines: multiplicity_eq_of_dvd_of_not_dvd for v2 (4,1) = 2, pow_v2_mul_T for T (1,y) = (1,1), quotient_two_of_parity for B/2B. Give the master the l.51 observation as evidence for OQ-42 (a).

The claim is true: 3y+1 = 2ᵏ·(−1/3) with −1/3 odd. The proof even computes it, as the first component of T_unique, then discards it. Still, a finding that goes to the author should not cite a declaration for a fact it does not state.

notes: There is no major finding. All three labels are unmarked and partial, which matches their status. The Lean statements are at least the printed ones under the disclosed readings (ℤ₂ for A₂; IsZ2Ring for 'ℤ/2ℤ-ring'). The three paper findings are true and faithfully formalized. theo:rep is false on 2ℤ₂+1 whatever completion of p_n is chosen. The printed proof does not argue surjectivity, and the Lean proves it. The second corollary fails at i = j and holds for i ≠ j under both OQ-43 readings, non-vacuously. On the dispatch's marking question: keep cor:ring_following_equivalent_enumerate unmarked. It depends on OQ-42 (a), as minor finding 1 shows (false for ℤ × ℤ/3ℤ), and on OQ-42 (d), since a codomain-respecting completion at −1/3 breaks it (argued). Under integrality, and wherever the paper's maps are defined, it is the printed statement in every reading of 'periodic of period n'. Once both rulings are made, periodic_a_iff_periodic_T certifies it unchanged. Rep.lean can graduate with or without the two minor fixes; neither changes a statement anyone relies on.
